clue.text: Constant drinker in the end, this writer's nose mostly turning red

indicators.note: turning round makes the letters run the opposite way
most but not all of something means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: c is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: final letter of drinker
the setter speaking of themself: this writer is = I am = I'M
NOSE loses its last letter, then NOS is turned round

explanation.surface: A heavy drinker's nose slowly reddening over the years, as the setter ruefully admits of their own.
explanation.walkthrough: C, R and I'M build the front; NOSE trimmed to NOS and turned gives SON, making CRIMSON.
explanation.definitionFit: Crimson is a deep shade of red, so the colour word is a direct synonym here.

clue.text: Lie with nothing on for picture

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring
a story is a fib or untruth

explanation.surface: Someone lying naked while posing for a painting.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'with nothing on' puts the zero on top of the lie; love is zero in tennis. 'Picture' here means a film, not a painting.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture is a cinema film, and a romantic movie is commonly called a love story.

clue.text: Kindly 6 Down, maybe one with good name

parts.note: the answer to 6 Down is ELTON, and Ben Elton is a British comedian and writer
the Roman numeral for one
standard abbreviation for good
standard abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A kindly Elton with a good reputation.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference points at ELTON, which seems to lead to Elton John; the other famous Elton is the comedian Ben Elton, supplying his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Benign means gentle and well-meaning, the same sense as kindly used as an adjective.

clue.text: Sheep fold in front of church — it's not worth much

parts.note: a tup is a ram
a sheepfold is an enclosure or pen
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A humble sheep enclosure outside a church, valued at next to nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In front of' just places the pen before the church letters. Tuppence is two old British pennies.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuppence, two pence, is a proverbially tiny sum, as in not caring tuppence about something.

clue.text: Running wildly, no hero, cat character in film

indicators.note: running about out of control, the letters scatter into a new order

parts.note: fifteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A big cat fleeing in a panic, no hero at all, in a film scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wildly' looks like the anagram signal but it is part of the fodder. The surface also describes the character: a cat who is no hero.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cowardly Lion is a character in the 1939 film The Wizard of Oz, played by Bert Lahr.

clue.text: Pressure's on richest out-of-form baseball players

indicators.note: something out of form has lost its proper shape, so the letters lose their order

parts.note: p is the symbol for pressure
seven letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Pressure mounting on wealthy ballplayers going through a bad patch.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'is on' puts P on top of the reshuffled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In baseball the pitchers are the players who throw the ball to the batter.

clue.text: Some misspelt onomatopoeia for John?

indicators.note: some of the words means only a portion of their letters, a run inside them

parts.note: the run straddles the two words

explanation.surface: Someone wondering whether a badly spelt sound-word is the work of a John.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across misspELT ONomatopoeia. The question mark warns that John is defined by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Elton is the given name famously paired with John, the singer Elton John.

clue.text: You may need a rest before you address me

definitions.text: You may need a rest before you address me

parts.words: You may need a rest before you address me
parts.note: surface reading: a tiring person you must recover from before speaking to them

parts.words: You may need a rest before you address me
parts.note: setter's reading: at snooker the rest is a cue support, and you address the white ball before striking

explanation.walkthrough: In snooker and billiards a rest is a stick that supports the cue for awkward shots, and to address the ball is to line up to hit it.
explanation.definitionFit: The white ball struck by the cue is the one players line up on, sometimes using a rest for reach.

clue.text: A little aggro overcoming Slot

indicators.note: a little of the following words means only a short stretch of their letters is used

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A small bit of aggression winning a place in the team.
explanation.walkthrough: The run is agGRO OVErcoming. Slot looks like a verb or a place, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A groove is a narrow channel or slit cut into a surface, which is one meaning of slot.

clue.text: Around the back of hotel, new dinette given a name

indicators.note: to be around something is to surround it on both sides
something new has been remade, so the letters take a fresh order
the back of a word is its last letter

parts.note: last letter of hotel
seven letters rearranged, which then wrap the single letter

explanation.surface: A small dining area at the rear of a hotel being given a fancy name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dinette' looks like the thing being named, but its letters are the anagram material, wrapped around the hotel's last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To entitle something is to give it a title, so entitled means named.

clue.text: One liable to forget a million counterfeit in case

indicators.note: a counterfeit is a fake, something made up, so the letters are made into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
standard abbreviation for million
six letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A forger who might forget a million in fake notes stashed in a suitcase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In case' looks like a phrase meaning 'just in case', but its six letters are the anagram material.
explanation.definitionFit: An amnesiac suffers memory loss, so is a person prone to forgetting things.

clue.text: Tough guy keeping close to Wimbledon tennis player

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside

parts.note: a he-man is a macho tough guy

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, its last letter

parts.note: last letter of Wimbledon

explanation.surface: A tough competitor hanging on near Wimbledon, the home of tennis.
explanation.walkthrough: HE-MAN takes N in the middle: HE + N + MAN. Tim Henman was a British tennis star famed for long Wimbledon runs.
explanation.definitionFit: Tim Henman was a leading British player, so the surname fits as an example of a tennis professional.

clue.text: Potential answer in questionnaire beats me

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the box ticked when a survey respondent has no opinion
second meaning: a casual way of saying one has no idea

explanation.surface: A respondent baffled by a survey question.
explanation.walkthrough: Both halves name the same reply: a standard survey option, and what someone says when stumped.
explanation.definitionFit: Surveys offer an option for respondents unsure of their view, and the same phrase expresses everyday ignorance.

clue.text: Dog show with Winton, possibly on fourth of June

parts.note: to air something is to show it publicly

indicators.note: the fourth of a word picks its fourth letter alone

parts.note: fourth letter of June
Dale Winton was a British TV presenter, so his first name is one possibility

explanation.surface: A dog show hosted by Dale Winton, perhaps held in early June.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' places DALE after the E. Dale Winton hosted the British game show Supermarket Sweep.
explanation.definitionFit: The Airedale is a large terrier breed from Yorkshire, so it is one kind of dog.

clue.text: Fan tended to dither about one facing allegations

indicators.note: dithering about means moving to and fro indecisively, so the letters are shaken up

parts.note: nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A supporter who tends to waver over someone accused of wrongdoing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fan' and 'tended' read as subject and verb but together they are the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A defendant is the person in court against whom charges or claims are brought.

clue.text: Bookish intellectuals half-heartedly refuse a note

indicators.note: with only half a heart, one of the two central letters is dropped

parts.note: litter is rubbish, refuse; one of its middle Ts goes
taken as written
ti is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Snobbish scholars grudgingly declining a written message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like a verb but it is the noun meaning rubbish; LITTER loses one central T to give LITER.
explanation.definitionFit: Literati are well-read, educated people interested in literature, a learned elite.

clue.text: I think one mike in rock opera is missing — take heed

indicators.note: something missing has gone, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: Tommy is the rock opera by The Who; mike is M in the NATO alphabet, and one of its two Ms goes
to mind is to pay attention

explanation.surface: A performer convinced a microphone has gone missing from a rock opera production, warning everyone to watch out.
explanation.walkthrough: Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet; the rock opera's title has two of them, and 'one' tells you only a single M goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'to my mind' introduces a personal opinion, exactly as 'I think' does.

clue.text: Working with Brown, as Marge might be

parts.note: a machine that is on is working
to toast bread is to brown it

explanation.surface: Marge, perhaps Marge Simpson, working alongside someone called Brown.
explanation.walkthrough: Marge looks like a woman's name; here it is short for margarine, the spread.
explanation.definitionFit: Margarine is typically spread over a slice of grilled bread, so that is where it might be found.

clue.text: Lucky charms Rod's holding firm

indicators.note: to hold something is to have it in one's grasp, inside

parts.note: a mast is a pole or rod, plus the S
CO is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: Rod clinging to his lucky charms with a firm grip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' reads as an adjective for the grip, but it is the noun meaning company.
explanation.definitionFit: A mascot is a person, animal or object believed to bring good luck.

clue.text: Where gamblers are attracted to young female boxing star

indicators.note: boxing something in means enclosing it

parts.note: a lass is a girl
Vega is a bright star in the constellation Lyra

explanation.surface: Punters drawn to watch a young woman boxing star fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxing star' looks like a sporting celebrity; boxing is the container signal and the star is Vega.
explanation.definitionFit: Las Vegas in Nevada is famous worldwide for its casinos and gambling resorts.

clue.text: Sign percussion instrument can be heard

indicators.note: what can be heard is what is spoken, so the sound matters, not the spelling

parts.note: a cymbal is a brass percussion plate

explanation.surface: A sign that a percussion instrument is audible.
explanation.walkthrough: Cymbal and symbol are pronounced identically.
explanation.definitionFit: A symbol is a mark or token that stands for something, the same as a sign.

clue.text: Could this be standing, mostly, on sculpture's base?

definitions.text: Could this be standing, mostly, on sculpture's base?

indicators.note: most of something means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: status is standing or rank; it loses its final letter

indicators.note: the base of a word is its bottom, its final letter

parts.note: last letter of sculpture

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a figure standing on a plinth is the sculpture itself.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition as well as the wordplay: STATU then E, and a statue does stand on a base.
explanation.definitionFit: A statue is a carved or cast figure, typically upright and mounted on a pedestal.

clue.text: Old king preceding old queen's coach

parts.note: Tutankhamun, the ancient Egyptian pharaoh, is known as King Tut
standard abbreviation for old
R for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A historical royal procession: an ancient king's carriage ahead of a former queen's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coach' looks like a carriage to go with the royals, but it is the verb-turned-noun for a teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutor gives private instruction, just as a coach trains a pupil.

clue.text: Useless type hit Crouch after header for England

parts.note: to lam is to thrash or hit

indicators.note: the header of a word is its first letter, at its head

parts.note: first letter of England
to duck is to crouch down

explanation.surface: Peter Crouch, the England striker, scoring with a header and a hopeless player being taken to task.
explanation.walkthrough: Crouch evokes the tall England footballer Peter Crouch; here it simply means duck. 'After' places DUCK after the E.
explanation.definitionFit: A lame duck is an idiom for an ineffective or failing person or thing.

clue.text: Spicy beef is tapas bar's last piece? I'm devastated!

indicators.note: something devastated is wrecked, its parts thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the last piece of a word is its final letter

parts.note: last letter of bar
taken as written

explanation.surface: A diner devastated to find the tapas bar has served its last portion of spicy beef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'm devastated' reads as a cry of dismay; the I'M joins TAPAS and R as the anagram material.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastrami is cured, seasoned and smoked beef, usually spiced with pepper and coriander.

clue.text: Decorated knight's boring talk

indicators.note: to bore is to drill into, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: to orate is to make a speech
N is the chess notation for knight; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A decorated knight who delivers tedious speeches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' looks like 'tedious' but means drilling into. 'Decorated' suggests honours for the knight; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ornate is elaborately adorned with decoration.

clue.text: Celebrities occasionally singing Aquarius?

parts.note: famous people are stars

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: Famous people now and then performing the song Aquarius from the musical Hair.
explanation.walkthrough: Aquarius suggests the hit song; the question mark shows it is an example of a zodiac sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Aquarius is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac, each called a star sign.
